title: Improving the microclimate in urban areas: a case study in the centre of Athens
journal: Building Services Engineering Research and Technology
outcome: Combined cool pavements + green spaces + solar control + earth-to-air heat exchangers on 4160 m2 square; cool pavement surface up to 4.8C cooler than asphalt (measured); local summer air temp decrease up to 2C
design: Pre/post field monitoring campaigns of implemented bioclimatic rehabilitation + CFD-assisted evaluation
source_review: Urban Climate 2023 cool pavements systematic review (Table 5); also Akbari et al. 2016 JCEM

title: Bioclimatic design of open public spaces in the historic centre of Tirana, Albania
outcome: 25000 m2 bioclimatic rehabilitation combining IR-reflective cool pavements + greenery + shading; pavement surface up to 8C cooler (measured); ambient -2.1C (model-estimated)
design: Implemented urban regeneration with surface/microclimate monitoring + simulation
source_review: Urban Climate 2023 cool pavements systematic review; Akbari et al. 2016 JCEM

title: Cool roofs and cool pavements application in Acharnes, Greece
outcome: Combined cool roofs (municipal building) + cool paving stones (square/sidewalk); pavement surface -10K (measured); 17% annual cooling energy demand reduction
design: Field monitoring (meteorological, surface temp, thermal imaging) of implemented measures + EnergyPlus/ENVI-met models
source_review: Urban Climate 2023 cool pavements systematic review (Table 5)

title: The evaluation of the temperature reduction effects of cool roofs and cool pavements as urban heatwave mitigation strategies
outcome: Combined cool roofs + cool pavements installed district-wide; roof surface -15.5C avg (max 22.9C), indoor air -2.7C; pavement surface -1.8 to -5.8C (parking) and -2.5 to -4.3C (alleys)
design: Field experiment with thermal imaging + temperature loggers at 6 roof sites and multiple pavement sites

title: Exploring the heat mitigation effects of urban climate adaptation facilities
outcome: Combined program: cooling fog -3.1C ambient; cool roofs -2 to -3C surface; shading structures -10C surface; small water paths -1.5C air; WBGT/UTCI comfort improved
design: Multi-year (2021-2023) field deployment with continuous IoT sensor monitoring across four cities

title: Heat island mitigation using water retentive pavement sprinkled with reclaimed wastewater
outcome: Water-retentive pavement + reclaimed wastewater sprinkling; road surface -8C daytime and -3C night; sensible-to-latent heat flux shift; WBGT measured
design: Field survey comparing sprinkled vs non-sprinkled areas of implemented system
source_review: Cited in Hendel 2016 pavement-watering thesis lit review; verified via doi.org record

title: Measuring the effects of urban heat island mitigation techniques in the field: application to the case of pavement-watering in Paris
outcome: Operational street pavement-watering (city cleaning water network); field-measured air temperature, humidity and UTCI thermal comfort improvements at watered vs control streets
design: Paired watered/control street field monitoring over summers 2013-2014
source_review: Hendel 2016 PhD thesis (fetched) and citing record pages

title: The cooling efficiency of urban landscape strategies in a hot dry climate
outcome: Six combined treatments of trees + lawn + shade mesh in courtyards; shade trees + grass gave daytime air temp depression up to 2.5K; shading grass cut irrigation water >50% (synergy)
design: Paired semi-enclosed courtyard field experiment, summer season
source_review: Cited (with 2011 companion) in Akbari et al. 2016 JCEM review; abstract fetched

title: Influence of tree cover on summertime surface energy balance fluxes, San Gabriel Valley, Los Angeles
outcome: Paired neighborhoods with 30% vs 10% irrigated tree/shrub cover; higher latent heat flux but also higher net radiation and slightly higher ambient temps at high-tree site
design: Simultaneous two-site surface energy balance field campaign (18 clear-sky summer days)
source_review: Santamouris et al. 2018 JCEM greenery review (combined-technologies section)

title: Evidence-based guidance on reflective pavement for urban heat mitigation in Arizona
outcome: 58 km reflective pavement seal (city pilot); surface -8.4C max at noon but mean radiant temp +2.3 to +5.1C midday; minimal air temp change; albedo degraded over 7 months
design: Micrometeorological comparison of three treated vs untreated neighborhoods

title: An observation on the climatic effect of watering on paved roads
journal: Journal of Hydroscience and Hydraulic Engineering
outcome: Road watering using preexisting snow-melting pipe infrastructure; observed cooling of paved road surfaces and local climate during hot weather
design: Field observation of watered vs unwatered paved road sections
source_review: Hendel 2016 PhD thesis pavement-watering literature review (fetched)

title: Study on appropriate heat mitigation technologies for urban block redevelopment based on demonstration experiments in Kobe city
outcome: Measured effects of implemented measures: road watering cut surface temp ~10C / MRT 1.9C / SET* 0.8C; fractal sunshade+mist cut MRT ~15C and SET* ~7C; water surface cut surface temp ~15C
design: Field demonstration experiments of five implemented heat countermeasures evaluated with SET*

title: Restoration of an inner-city stream and its impact on air temperature and humidity based on long-term monitoring data
outcome: Long-term monitored air temperature and humidity changes around Cheonggyecheon after stream restoration (highway removal + water + greenway)
design: Before-after long-term station monitoring of implemented urban stream restoration

title: Influence of urban form on the cooling effect of a small urban river
outcome: Restored Cheonggye River mean cooling intensity 0.46C over 32.7 m at 2pm and 0.37C over 37.2 m at 10pm; modulated by street width and building height
design: Summer field transect measurements around implemented restored urban river
source_review: full-text PDF fetched from DTU Orbit repository

title: Thermal comfort and energy performance of a passive urban climate shelter under extreme heat: Large-scale measurements at Cartuja Qanat Agora
outcome: Implemented shelter combining solar blocking + water-fed radiant ceiling + ground/water heat exchange + evaporative night regeneration cut outdoor air temp >15C and MRT up to 8C; 80% of users thermally neutral
design: Large-scale experimental monitoring plus user comfort surveys of implemented multi-technology urban climate shelter
source_review: ScienceDirect via doi.org and Univ. of Seville repository

title: Evaluating the effect of green, blue, and gray measures for climate change adaptation on children's well-being in schoolyards in Barcelona
outcome: After green + blue (fountains) + gray (shade) schoolyard transformations in 11 schools: reduced heat sensation and improved comfort vs 10 comparison schools
design: Pre-post quasi-experimental difference-in-differences evaluation of implemented interventions

title: Spatial Microclimatic Characterization of a Parisian 'Oasis' Schoolyard
journal: Proceedings of the 5th International Conference on Building Energy and Environment (Springer)
outcome: Microclimatic performance of implemented unsealed and greened OASIS schoolyard vs paired control, before (2019) and after (2021) works
design: BACI design with fixed weather stations plus mobile summer campaigns
source_review: cited in arXiv 2408.08317 ref [24]; abstract fetched via doi.org
